purpose: External eval set for vibe-planning. Coverage focuses on plan-only boundaries, fixture-grounded and evidence-labeled plan artifacts, localized summaries, bug and restoration proof, investigation adequacy, derived values and discriminating metrics, test selection by open obligation, explicit checkpoints and resumable progress, spec approval evidence, durable decision records, human verification cost, and bounded delegated review.
coverage_notes: Full-artifact cases (display-name, unreproduced bug report, resumable multi-slice, planning-only stop, restoration, broad UX, derived limit, and About dialog release-notes) carry the complete plan workflow: artifact capture, section order, evidence labels, tests before steps, handoff, self-review, and the concise summary. Response-only cases (handed-off contradictory spec, credential rotation, concurrent composition, review-driven revision, migration proof, unknown capacity, offline-mode decision index, human verification cost, and token-expiry reviewer comment) pressure one realistic scenario each, possibly combining several contracts of that scenario, while keeping ambient-repository investigation and artifact construction out of the measurement; each keeps a creates-no-artifact guard where the full workflow would tempt a write. The handed-off-spec case cannot exercise a genuine out-of-band orchestration record; it only checks that a prompt-contained claim stays inert. The About dialog release-notes and token-expiry reviewer-comment cases are the test-selection cases ADR-0010 names. Contracts whose assertions were non-discriminating in both configurations (output-language variable precedence, external-claim proof, paired visibility proof, universal bounds, enumeration authority, criterion coherence, invariant metrics, reserved decisions, hypothetical orchestration handoff) keep their skill text but no dedicated case.
common_assertions: Output is planning-only: it writes or names only plan artifacts and the decision records or findings report entries the planning contract declares as supporting paths, does not edit implementation or other repository support files, and leaves plan changes uncommitted unless the current user explicitly requests a commit.
